scenes.title: Three Days Left
scenes.summary: Sunday morning in the café corner: F1 and F2 calm M2 down and divide the tasks needed before Wednesday at three.
scenes.intro: On Sunday morning at {SHOW}, {M2} paces beside the breakfast counter with three pages of worried notes while {F1} and {F2} pour coffee and plan the week. Listen to the scene first.
story: Sunday, Monday, Tuesday—and Wednesday at three o'clock the city clerk walks in!
Sit down and drink your hot coffee before you spill it, {M2}.
Look at our whiteboard: three days, three simple jobs.
Only three jobs?! Yesterday Room Nine was full of dust and silent piano keys!
Sunday: wash every window and read your aunt's old green guest book.
Monday: paint the outside shutters warm green and arrange twelve chairs.
Tuesday: repair the silent piano key and bake Wednesday's lemon tarts!
When you divide a mountain into three small hills, I can breathe again!
Where did you put that old green guest book from the attic, {M2}?
Right here under my arm! Wait—where did I put my coffee cup?
Go rest for ten minutes, boss—{F1} and {F3} will read the book!
scenes.outro: Three days, three clear steps, and {M2}'s aunt's green guest book is finally on the table. See you in the next scene.

scenes.title: The Green Guest Book
scenes.summary: F1, F3, and M2 turn to May thirty years ago in the green guest book and learn why the Friday concert stopped.
scenes.intro: At the sunny corner table, {F3} puts on her reading glasses beside {F1} and {M2} and opens the cloth-bound green ledger to May thirty years ago. Let's listen in first.
story: Look how neat every page is: date, room number, guest name, and weather.
Turn to May tenth, {F3}—the Friday written on our postcard!
Here it is! 'Heavy rain all night; water dripped onto the sunroom piano.'
Read the next line: 'Moved the piano to the dry corner; middle key swollen shut.'
Oh! That rainy night broke the roof and jammed middle D at the same time!
Look at my aunt's note underneath: 'Locked Room Nine until the roof is dry.'
And she tucked her unfinished waltz inside the lid to wait for sunny weather!
Then summer guests filled the house, years passed, and the bookcase went up.
She never got to hear the second half of her Friday waltz.
{M2}, with your permission, may I write the missing sixteen bars for Wednesday?
You would finish my aunt's song for our reopening, {F3}?!
In the very same key, with her opening melody leading us home.
scenes.outro: The mystery of the locked sunroom and the unfinished page is solved—and {F3} offers to complete the waltz for Wednesday's reopening. See you next time.

scenes.title: Inside the Piano Action
scenes.summary: M1 opens the front panel of the upright piano with F3 and M3 and spots a slipped brass hinge pin on middle D.
scenes.intro: In Room 9, {M1} kneels beside his tool kit and carefully lifts off the front wooden panel of the upright piano while {F3} and {M3} watch the row of felt hammers inside. Listen first.
story: I have fixed boilers, locks, and clocks, madam, but never a piano.
A piano is just honest wood, wool felt, and steel wire, {M1}.
Press the key to the left first so we see how a healthy hammer moves.
Watch C rise smoothly and strike the three strings—clean and bright.
Now press the silent key right next to it.
Look: the key goes down, but the little wooden hammer leans sideways!
Shine the lamp closer—the tiny brass hinge pin slipped half out of the wood!
Wait... nothing is cracked! The damp air thirty years ago only loosened the felt bushing!
Can you seat a tiny pin that small without splitting the beechwood, {M1}?
Give me quiet light, thin tweezers, and dry glue tomorrow morning.
Once that hammer stands straight, {F3} can tune the whole middle octave?
Do you have a tuning key in the chest, {M1}? Look in the bottom drawer!
scenes.outro: No cracked wood—just one slipped brass pin waiting for {M1}'s steady hands. Let's see what else is in the chest next time.

scenes.title: Soap, Buckets, and Sunlight
scenes.summary: F1, M3, and M4 wash thirty years of dust off the tall arched sunroom glass with warm soapy water.
scenes.intro: Sunday afternoon arrives, and {F1}, {M3}, and {M4} roll up their sleeves inside Room 9 with two buckets of warm soapy water and clean cotton cloths. Listen first.
story: Take the lower panes, {F1}; {M3} and I can reach the top arch from the ladder.
Dip the sponge in warm water with a drop of vinegar—zero streaks on old glass!
Whoa, look at that first square I wiped! Blue sky and green leaves!
Remember when mom made us wash the kitchen windows every spring, {M3}?
You always splashed water on my shirt and blamed the wind!
Careful up there, you two—keep the soapy water in the bucket!
Look through the clean glass now: you can see the whole courtyard lantern line!
When we open the outside shutters tomorrow, sunlight will pour across all four tables.
Wait—{M3}, didn't you say your train home leaves tonight at seven?
I called my studio partner and moved my ticket to Saturday morning.
Really?! You are staying in {CITY} until Friday's opening night?!
Nothing could pull me away before Room Nine opens!
scenes.outro: Clean arched glass lets the courtyard green shine in, and {M3} extends his stay through opening night! See you next time.

scenes.title: Stuck Shutters Outside
scenes.summary: Outside in the courtyard, M1, F1, and M2 oil the rusty hinges on Room 9's exterior wooden shutters and swing them wide open.
scenes.intro: Stepping out onto the courtyard stones, {M1}, {F1}, and {M2} stand before the four tall wooden shutters on the side wall that have stayed latched for thirty years. Let's listen in first.
story: Funny—I walked past these grey shutters every morning and stopped seeing them!
Because the climbing ivy grew right across the middle iron hook!
Don't cut the vine, {F1}; lift the green branch gently onto the trellis.
Look! All the leaves stay safe, and now we can reach the iron latch!
Let me pull—ugh! It will not budge a single millimetre!
Oil first, muscle second, boss. Two drops on each hinge pin.
Give the oil ten seconds... now lift slightly and pull together!
One, two—there goes the left shutter!
And the right one! Look how big the courtyard looks with glass on two sides!
Wave through the clean window—{F3} is smiling at the piano inside!
We definitely need fresh green paint on this dry grey wood tomorrow.
Sandpaper tonight, green paint Monday morning—if the sky stays dry.
scenes.outro: With two drops of oil and the ivy safely tucked onto the trellis, Room 9's tall windows open onto the courtyard for the first time in decades. See you next time.

scenes.title: Sixteen Missing Bars
scenes.summary: At dusk on Sunday, F3 hums and pencils two possible endings for the waltz while F1 and M3 listen over hot mint tea.
scenes.intro: As Sunday dusk turns the courtyard lanterns gold, {F3} sits at the sunroom table with music paper and a soft pencil while {M3} carries in hot mint tea from the kitchen for {F1} and {F3}. Listen first.
story: {F2} sent hot mint tea and warm almond biscuits for our composer!
Thank you both. Listen while I tap two rhythms on the table.
Does the ending go fast and bright, or gentle and slow?
{M2}'s aunt wrote a light dancing beginning, like morning footsteps.
Then in the middle, the melody climbs up like afternoon conversation!
Exactly! So at six in the evening, how should a Friday waltz end?
Warm and unhurried—like friends lingering over their last cup of tea.
Yes! Repeat the opening four notes softly, one octave higher, and come home.
Just hearing you hum it in this glass room sounds wonderful, {F3}!
Wait—right in bar twenty-eight, the melody lands squarely on middle D!
The exact silent key {M1} is repairing tomorrow morning!
No pressure for poor {M1}—the whole song rests on his tweezers!
scenes.outro: {F3} has pencilled a warm evening ending—and its key moment lands right on middle D! See you next time.

scenes.title: Testing the Café Menu
scenes.summary: In the kitchen corner, F2 asks brothers M3 and M4 to taste two versions of her Wednesday café soup and lemon tart.
scenes.intro: Later Sunday evening in the café corner, {F2} sets out small tasting bowls and two slices of tart for {M3} and {M4}. Let's listen in first.
story: Every good neighbourhood café needs one hot lunch bowl and one signature cake.
Did we just get promoted to official taste testers, {M3}?
Best job in the building! Which bowl do we try first, {F2}?
Left spoon: roasted tomato soup with fresh courtyard herbs.
Rich, warm, and great with crusty bread on a rainy afternoon!
Right spoon: golden lentil soup with lemon and olive oil—even better!
Now try the two lemon tart slices: thin pastry on the left, almond crust on the right.
Oh—the almond crust with Saturday market lemon is unbeatable!
Save one slice for {M1}, {F2}, or he will lock us out of the kitchen!
So Wednesday's menu is set: golden lentil soup, warm bread, almond lemon tart, and tea!
Simple, honest, and easy to serve quickly from noon to evening.
Now let us hope for sunny skies tomorrow so our shutter paint dries!
scenes.outro: Golden lentil soup and almond lemon tart win unanimous approval—leaving Monday morning's shutter painting next on the list. Final scene of Episode 3 coming up.

scenes.title: Thunder at Midnight
scenes.summary: While closing up on Sunday night, F1 and M1 hear sudden thunder and rush to pull the newly sanded shutters under cover before a downpour.
scenes.intro: Just before midnight on Sunday, {F1} is locking the cash drawer at the front desk while {M1} checks his brass keys—when a low rumble shakes the courtyard glass. Listen first.
story: Did a heavy truck just drive down {STREET}, {M1}?
No trucks at midnight. Look through the lobby glass—lightning!
Oh no! You took all four wooden shutters off their hinges after sanding them!
And they are leaning bare against the courtyard wall right now!
If bare dry wood gets soaked tonight, Monday's green paint will never stick!
Grab the back door lantern, {F1}—first big drops are already falling!
I have the left end of shutter one—lift and run for the hallway!
Good! Two down, two more outside—watch the wet stones!
Got the last pair just as the sky opened up! Whew, my sleeves are soaked!
The wood is bone-dry, {F1}. You move fast in a storm.
Wait—if it pours all day Monday, where do we paint four tall shutters?!
Look at our Monday forecast... heavy rain until Tuesday noon!
scenes.outro: {F1} and {M1} rescue the bare wooden shutters seconds before midnight rain pours down—but with rain forecast all Monday, how will the paint dry before Wednesday?! Episode 3 is complete—see you in Episode 4.
